### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 44a030bfc8b1a3e1b5b6a4518e89831858b9c452` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6c77f9a8eac6321c65f17294f649f55b7543b411` — the merge of head `7b59e0068d1b817ad06c26be00fc06a5551afc1b` into base `44a030bfc8b1a3e1b5b6a4518e89831858b9c452`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6c77f9a8eac6321c65f17294f649f55b7543b411 && git checkout 6c77f9a8eac6321c65f17294f649f55b7543b411
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 44a030bfc8b1a3e1b5b6a4518e89831858b9c452 7b59e0068d1b817ad06c26be00fc06a5551afc1b && git checkout -B drift-repro 44a030bfc8b1a3e1b5b6a4518e89831858b9c452 && git merge --no-ff 7b59e0068d1b817ad06c26be00fc06a5551afc1b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 44a030bfc8b1a3e1b5b6a4518e89831858b9c452
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7b59e0068d1b817ad06c26be00fc06a5551afc1b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-bare-name-conflict.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts, packages/core/src/kernel.ts, packages/core/src/security/guest-organization.ts

Reviewed on the narrowing face (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset; no published schema or governed path in the tree). Inputs: card #31296 with comments 6714782060, 6717053629, 6717747337; PR #31388 (body, three files, three commits aecae3be / fa466016 / 7b59e006), the net diff against `main` (merge-base 8b904420; `origin/main` at 44a030bf, 12 commits past it, none touching a cited file); the #30803 series on `main` (PRs #30836, #31006, #31093 merged; #31375 open at a9d8e397); the check-runs on this head. Read with `git show` / `git diff`; the checkout's ref was not moved; nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on 7b59e006 at record time**: 47 runs — 30 success, 13 skipped, 4 still `in_progress` (Test Core 1/8, 2/8, 3/8, 4/8). None failed. Complete and green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, Test Core 5/8–8/8, all four Type Check lanes (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), every Lint lane (ESLint; docs & code guards, which carries the ADR-0087 registration check; CI, release & engine gates; repo & tooling gates; PM dispatch-gates; the three scoped lanes), Test UI, Live E2E UI, Flag docs affected. The four open shards are the queue guard's to wait on; this record does not pre-empt them.

### ① Derived judgments

**The accept-set change, read in the catch (plugin.ts, step 3 of the cloud branch, `pr/31388` lines 2903–2941).** When `manifestService.register(...)` throws and `inlineManifest` is false, the catch now asks `refusesEnvironmentHeldCatalogName(err) || refusesBareNameHeldElsewhere(err)`. When the second arm answers yes the door returns `422` with `code: 'PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED'` and `message: Package '…' cannot be installed: ` plus the registry's own sentence — the same body shape and status the #25366 arm already returned. Before this head that refusal fell through to #22695's lenient path: `hotLoadError` set, ledger entry written at step 4 (`this.ledger.write(entry)`, line 2964), `200` with `hotLoaded: false`. So the cloud-branch installs now refused are exactly those whose register the registry refuses with `BareNameConflictError`; every other register failure on that branch (including `NamespaceConflictError`, which shares the code but not the name) keeps the lenient answer, as the PR states.

**Both holders and the rename are in the answer.** The message is the registry's: `BareNameConflictError`'s constructor (registry.ts 2843–2880) joins one `bareNameConflictLine` per conflict — `package "incoming" declares the flow "name", already held by package "holder" — rename it to "ns_name" in "incoming"` — followed by `bareNameReason` and the remedy (rename in either package, or uninstall one; for a built-in holder, rename only). The test's `expectBareNameRefusal` asserts both package ids, the name and `routing_assign_technician` in the message, plus `BaseResponseSchema` / `ApiErrorSchema` / `envelopeViolations` on the envelope.

**Nothing is written or hot-loaded on refusal.** The return is before step 4 (ledger write, 2964), 4b (`syncSchemas`), 4b′ (datasources), 4c (`bindArtifactHandlers`, 3000) and 5 (`applySideEffects`, 3007). Steps 2c–2e before the register are gates that return refusals; the cloud fetch (line 2249) is a read; the door writes nothing of its own before step 3. On the registry's side `installPackage` (registry.ts 8655–8690) runs `refuseBareNameConflicts` ahead of `const now = …` and every record write, so a refused package leaves no package record, no claim and no items — the PR's "the registry's package door already refused before its own writes" holds. The test pins ledger equality before/after for both ids, `getPackage(INCOMING_ID)` undefined (fresh) or still `1.0.0` (upgrade), and the holder's flow label unchanged.

**An environment-held catalog name keeps its answer.** The #25366 predicate is unchanged (lines 379–384) and sits first in the `||`; the new CONTROL registers a bare-slot permission set via `registry.registerItem` and asserts the `422` naming "the environment catalog". `installPackage` runs `refuseSecurityCatalogNameConflicts` (8671) before `refuseBareNameConflicts` (8690), so a package carrying both an environment-held catalog name and a held bare name is refused by the first throw, which the first arm recognises — `422` either way.

**A fresh name installs.** CONTROL: `v1-free` answers `200`, `hotLoaded: true`, no `hotLoadError`, registered and ledgered, the flow served under the incoming package's label, the holder's flow kept.

**The predicate is the error's brand, not a copy of the rule.** `refusesBareNameHeldElsewhere` reads `e?.code === NAMESPACE_CONFLICT_CODE && e.name === 'BareNameConflictError'` and nothing else: no `conflicts`, no `itemType`, no `existingHolder`, no list of types. `BareNameConflictError` sets `readonly code = NAMESPACE_CONFLICT_CODE` and `this.name = 'BareNameConflictError'` (registry.ts 2844, 2875); the class is exported from `registry.ts` but not from the package barrel (`index.ts` re-exports `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT_CODE` alone, line 83), so "unexported" and "compared rather than instanceof-tested" are accurate. The pair is the shape `isGuestOrganizationUnresolvedError` uses (core `security/guest-organization.ts` 92–96) and the `DuplicateRecordError` readers in `types/data-error-classification.ts` 820 and `metadata-protocol/protocol-client-failures.ts` 203. The siblings are told apart by name: `NamespaceConflictError` (same code, no match → lenient, as before) and `SecurityCatalogNameConflictError` (same code, matched only through the #25366 arm's `existingHolder.kind === 'environment'`).

**The brand reaches the catch unwrapped.** Traced on `main`: objectql `plugin.ts` `register` (883–980) converts, judges residuals, then calls `ql.registerApp(manifest, scope, source)` per entry with no try/catch; `engine.ts` 2168 delegates to `RegistrationFacet.registerApp`; `engine-registration.ts` `registerPackageBody` (233–240) calls `this._registry.installPackage(manifest, source, undefined, scope)` first, no try/catch; the facet's only try/catch (573) is the file-columns resolver, unrelated. The PR's own red run shows the un-wrapped sentence (`hotLoadError: "Bare-name conflict: package …"`) at the door.

**#31375 is covered without a type list.** Its patch to `bare-name-one-holder.ts` adds `'agent' | 'skill'` to `BareNameRegistryType` and the ordered list; its `registry.ts` hunks change neither `readonly code` nor `this.name`. Nothing here enumerates types or holders, so when #31375 lands the cloud branch refuses an agent or skill clash through the same arm.

**The doc-comment claims the hunks make, checked in the cited code.** (a) "rehydrated at the next boot BEFORE the cold boot seals the holders": `core/kernel.ts` `BOOT_PHASE_HOOKS = ['kernel:ready', 'kernel:bootstrapped', 'kernel:listening']`, triggered in that order (614, 626); install-local rehydrates inside its `kernel:ready` hook (plugin.ts 1551–1567); objectql seals in `kernel:bootstrapped` (plugin.ts 1228–1239, `sealBareNameHoldersAtColdBoot(registry, BARE_NAME_COLD_BOOT_MODE, …)`), whose own comment names "the install-local rehydrate at `kernel:ready`" as one of the registrations the seal waits for. Holds. (b) `BARE_NAME_COLD_BOOT_MODE = 'warn'` (bare-name-one-holder.ts 302) — the boot logs `bareNameColdBootWarning` once and "changes nothing about which holder each caller is served". Holds. (c) The module-header hunk's "another package (or the platform) holds a bare name" matches `BareNameHolder = package | built-in` (305–308). Holds.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/31296-install-local-cloud-bare-name-refused.md`: `'@objectstack/cloud-connection': patch`; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with the narrowed door, status and old answer spelled out ("Nothing is widened"); `Metadata-protocol: none`; the `**BREAKING**` banner; a Before / Now / Unchanged / Remedy body; `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with the reason (no schema key, no stored row read differently; the remedy is the rename the refusal names). The PR body carries the same `Clause-②` and `Metadata-protocol` lines and the `!` on the title. Under `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (ruling A, comments 895–925) `Metadata-protocol: none` grades every introduced entry `patch`; the `(narrowing)` arm keeps the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition and carries no level coupling; `narrowed` is not declared, so neither cross-check contradiction applies. The shape matches the `25921-*` narrowing changesets on `main`. Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard and Lint · docs & code guards (the ADR-0087 registration check) are complete and green on this head. The narrowing is honestly declared: #22695 left the lenient path lenient on purpose ("whether it should is a separate decision, ⛔ not made here"), so a `200` consumer could have relied on it; `patch` + `(narrowing)` + BREAKING is the correct level and declaration.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every flag in report 6717747337, answered or escalated:

- `out_of_scope_findings[0]` — the security catalog's refusal with a **package or built-in holder** still takes the lenient path on the cloud branch. Confirmed in the cited code: `refusesEnvironmentHeldCatalogName` keeps `existingHolder.kind === 'environment'` (plugin.ts 379–384); `refuseSecurityCatalogNameConflicts` (registry.ts 4423–4440) is guarded by `selfId === undefined` alone, no seal, and reads holders with `{ builtIns: true, environment: true }`; so the ledger entry written on the lenient path meets the same refusal at every rehydrate and the package never loads, while the answer said `200` "loads at the next restart" — and (per #25366's own comment in the catch) the earlier version's ledger entry it overwrote is lost too. Outside #31296's claimed predicate (the card's Expected names the bare-name refusal alone; the seat claim's file surface is the cloud branch's refusal predicate for it). **Escalated**: a new card for the server lane with the dev's dedupe words (`install-local security catalog package holder lenient`, `refusesEnvironmentHeldCatalogName package built-in`, `SecurityCatalogNameConflictError hotLoaded false`). Not a finding against this PR.
- Of the same shape, not in the report, read from code and not measured: `NamespaceConflictError` (registry.ts 8653, inside `installPackage`; same code, name `NamespaceConflictError`, no `conflicts`) also takes the lenient path on the cloud branch, and the namespace's owner is still installed at the next rehydrate, so that entry is refused at every boot too. **Escalated** for the same card or a sibling; outside this card's predicate.
- `deviations`: one merge of `origin/main` (8b904420) before the PR; `main` has moved 12 commits since. None touches `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`, `registry.ts`, `bare-name-one-holder.ts`, objectql `plugin.ts` or `kernel.ts` (checked with `git log 8b904420..origin/main -- …`). The PR reports `mergeable: true`. No re-merge owed for this review.
- "PR #31375 had not landed … no AI-family pin (seat note: not owed)": agreed — the predicate reads no type, #31375 leaves `code` and `name` as they are, and the AI family's own install-local pin is that PR's dogfood file to carry.
- `premise_still_valid: true`: confirmed on `origin/main` — the catch asks only `refusesEnvironmentHeldCatalogName(err)` (the diff's `-` line).
- `security_findings: none`, `mcp_calls: 0`, `api_writes: 2`, the card assignee untouched: no contract question here; not re-judged.
- The card's constraint "one predicate on that branch … never a copy of the holder rule": met (①).

### ④ Design judgment

**Does the narrowing take a declared capability away?** No. The capability the lenient path declares is "installed; the running kernel does not hold it; it loads at the next restart" (`hotLoaded: false` + `hotLoadError`, #22695). For a `BareNameConflictError` that promise is not a deferral but an evasion of the rule: the entry is rehydrated at `kernel:ready`, before the `kernel:bootstrapped` seal, and the boot under `'warn'` admits both holders and serves the name by registration order — the condition ADR-0048 §3.4 (narrowed, ruling C on #30798) and PRs #30836 / #31006 / #31093 were accepted to refuse. The inline branch of the same door already answers that refusal `422 PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED` (pinned on `main` in `packages/qa/dogfood/test/bare-name-one-holder.dogfood.test.ts` 163–181 and `…-flow-family.dogfood.test.ts` 205–220: "install-local of a third package declaring a held … name is 422 … nothing is installed"). The narrowing makes the series' own refusal real on the one door that lost it, with the registry's sentence and remedy, and leaves old ledger entries and every other register failure as they were. The remedy is the one the series published (rename to the namespaced name, or uninstall the other holder), so a consumer loses no path it was promised.

**Attempts to break it, each read in the tree:**

- *A refusal with both a bare-name and an environment holder.* An environment registration (no `packageId`) is never a bare-name holder (`BareNameHolder` is `package | built-in`; the item seam skips `packageId`-less registrations), so "both" means a package whose manifest trips both rules. `installPackage` throws the security catalog's refusal first (8671 before 8690); the first arm recognises it; `422`, nothing written. If a later reorder put the bare-name check first, the second arm recognises that throw instead. Holds either way.
- *A bundled member key (an email_template locale).* `declaredBareNames` declares a bundled type by its NAME ("two members of one bundle are one declaration, read twice"); the item seam judges `baseName`. The predicate reads neither names nor types, so whatever the registry decides arrives with the same brand. Holds.
- *A built-in holder.* `BUILT_IN_BARE_NAMES` is empty today; a future built-in produces the same class with `existingHolder.kind === 'built-in'` and the "a built-in name is never available to a package" remedy. The predicate does not read the holder. Holds.
- *An upgrade of the same package that already holds the name — must NOT be refused.* `bareNameHoldersOtherThan` (registry.ts 4678–4690) answers `[]` when `incomingPackageId` is already among the holders ("a reload, a re-install or an upgrade … is not a new holder"); the install-local upgrade path never calls `uninstallPackage` before the register (that verb is the uninstall route's, 3591), so the claims survive and no error is thrown — the predicate has nothing to recognise. Holds. The test's upgrade case re-declares the `v1` flow the package already holds and is refused for the OTHER name only, consistent with this; it does not assert the kept name is absent from the message — a nit, the rule is the registry's and pinned there.
- *The error thrown from a nested registration.* A nested plugin's collection reaches the item seam (`registerItem`, registry.ts 7647) and throws the same class; the path `registerPlugin → registerPackageBody → registerApp → manifest.register` has no catch, so the door answers `422` with nothing of its own written. The package door has already judged `plugins[]` one level deep (`declaredBareNames`), so the seam is a backstop; if it fires, the registry's record write (step 1 of `registerPackageBody`) has already happened — a registry-side concern that predates this PR and is identical on the inline branch; not this door's to fix.
- *Wrapped errors.* No wrapper on the path (①). A future `new Error(message)` wrap anywhere in it would drop `code` and `name` and silently restore the lenient answer — the exposure the #25366 arm already carries, and one the new test (a real `ObjectKernel` + `ObjectQLPlugin`, not a mocked `manifest`) would turn red.
- *A `function` clash (PR #31006's third type).* Not reachable at this door: a cloud-fetched manifest is JSON and carries no code functions (runtime `app-artifact-handlers.ts` 8; the request-family dogfood says so at line 26), and the hook binder's bind runs at step 4c after the ledger write, inside the binder's own try/catch, on both branches. Outside the card.
- *A `NamespaceConflictError`.* Same code, different name: not matched, lenient as before — correct for this card, escalated in ③ as the same class of false promise.

**Findings.** Must-fix: none. Should-fix: none. Nit (no effect on correctness or the contract): the new suite does not assert that the upgrade's kept name (`reassign_technician`, held by the package since `v1`) is absent from the `422` message; the registry's own suite pins that an upgrade is not a new holder.
